title: Ivonescimab plus chemotherapy improves survival in biliary tract cancer
content:
Results from the HARMONi-GI1 trial show that bispecifics challenge monoclonal antibodies in the first-line setting
The PD-1/VEGF bispecific antibody ivonescimab significantly improved outcomes for patients with advanced biliary tract cancer in a phase III trial presented at today’s Presidential Symposium at the ESMO Congress 2026 (Madrid, 23–27 October) ( LBA8 ).
In the HARMONi-GI1 trial , median overall survival (OS; primary endpoint) at a preplanned interim analysis was 14.9 months with ivonescimab plus chemotherapy compared with 12.1 months with the PD-L1 inhibitor durvalumab plus chemotherapy (hazard ratio [HR] 0.75; 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.61–0.92; p=0.0031). The study in 682 patients also met its key secondary endpoints, with significant improvements observed with ivonescimab in progression-free survival (PFS; HR 0.61; 95% CI 0.51–0.72; p<0.0001) and objective response rate (ORR; 53.8% versus 32.5%; p<0.0001). No new safety signals were identified.
“This is a pivotal study for the field , representing the fourth randomised phase III study in patients with treatment-naïve advanced biliary tract cancer to meet its primary overall survival endpoint,” states Dr James J. Harding from Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center, New York, USA.
Preclinical evidence for ivonescimab indicated that it displays cooperative binding to its targets, which may lead to enhanced potency ( iScience. 2024;28:111722 ). The bispecific showed encouraging antitumour activity when added to chemotherapy in an earlier phase II study in advanced biliary tract cancer ( J Hepatol. 2026; doi: 10.1016/j.jhep.2026.06.033 ).
HARMONi-GI1 was conducted exclusively in a Chinese population , representing a notable consideration for future study. “Hepatitis B infection rates were higher than those observed in prior global studies of patients with biliary tract cancer,” explains Harding. “Though the impact of these differences on the activity of immunotherapy is unclear, and through additional global testing, I hope the findings of HARMONi-GI1 will be an advance for the field.”
Biliary tract cancers are rare but molecularly diverse and precision medicine is already playing a part. Up to 50% of tumours have actionable genomic events that can be targeted with specific therapies and these have shown positive efficacy, particularly in disease possessing IDH1 and BRAF alterations, FGFR2 , NRG1 , NTRK and RET fusion/rearrangements, and HER2 overexpression ( J Hepatol . 2026;85:794–807 ). “I expect the list to grow in the next future, with KRAS allelic variants found in 17% of patients ( Clin Cancer Res. 2026;32:4166–4177 ), the next major target, and less common ones such as MTAP deletions and MET amplification are also being evaluated,” he adds.
The treatment shift toward bispecifics in this tumour type extends beyond ivonescimab, with several other agents now in development. Rilvegostomig, a PD-1/TIGIT antibody, is already undergoing head-to-head testing against durvalumab in a phase III first-line trial ( J Clin Oncol. 2026;44(Suppl 16):TPS4253 ). In the second-line setting, the DLL-4/VEGF antibody tovecimig has been reported to improve ORR and PFS .
Combination strategies will be important: a phase I study of ivonescimab with RAS inhibitors is already underway ( NCT07397388 ), and antibody–drug conjugates are being paired with immunotherapy, opening another route for bispecifics.

title: An anti-claudin 18.2 antibody-drug conjugate prolongs overall survival in gastroesophageal cancer
content:
Promising phase III results show a potential role of this drug class in pre-treated patients with advanced disease where the efficacy of current treatments is limited
At today’s Presidential Symposium at the ESMO Congress 2026 (Madrid, 23–27 October), the first phase III trial with a claudin 18.2 (CLDN18.2)-targeting antibody–drug conjugate (ADC) in gastro-oesophageal carcinoma showed positive overall survival (OS) results ( LBA7 ). The CLARITY-Gastric01 trial investigated sonesitatug vedotin (Sone-Ve) in 532 patients with advanced CLDN18.2-positive gastro-oesophageal carcinoma and had dual primary endpoints: OS in the third- or later-line setting and progression-free survival (PFS) in the second- and later-line setting (the intention-to-treat [ITT] population).
In the third- or later-line setting, median OS was 10.0 months in the Sone-Ve group versus 5.0 months in the investigator-choice group (hazard ratio [HR] 0.47; 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.36–0.62; p<0.000001) in 355 patients with CLDN18.2 expression on ≥25% of tumour cells at any staining intensity.
In the second- and later-line setting, median PFS did not meet the prespecified threshold for statistical significance with Sone-Ve compared with investigator’s choice of therapy (ITT: 4.2 months versus 3.8 months; HR 0.77; 95% CI 0.62–0.96; p=0.053). Median OS was significantly improved (10.6 months versus 6.4 months; HR 0.58; 95% CI 0.47–0.73; p=0.000004) in the ITT analysis, but subgroup analyses indicated that this may have been due to later-line effects (HR 0.47; 95% CI 0.36–0.62), rather than second-line benefits (HR 0.88; 95% CI 0.60–1.30). OS results were consistent across CLDN18.2 expression levels in the ITT population (≥25% to <75% expression and ≥75% expression).
The CLDN18.2 tight-junction protein is now a validated target in advanced gastric cancer given its common occurrence and based on results with the CLDN18.2-targeting monoclonal antibody, zolbetuximab, combined with chemotherapy in the first-line setting ( Nat Med. 2023;29:2133–2141 ; Lancet. 2023;401:1655–1668 ). “The CLARITY-Gastric01 findings are very promising, at least in patients who have had three or more lines of therapy,” says Prof. Salah-Eddin Al-Batran from Krankenhaus Nordwest, University Cancer Center Frankfurt and the Frankfurt Institute of Clinical Cancer Research, Germany. “Despite the rather complicated nature of dual primary endpoints in different settings in the trial, Sone-Ve could become an important new treatment option in the third- and later-line settings based on the doubling of median OS from 5 to 10 months. The situation in the second-line setting is less certain given the lack of a significant difference in PFS, but the safety profile is manageable,” he adds.
To what extent Sone-Ve will be active in patients who have already received zolbetuximab in the first-line setting is an intriguing question. Al-Batran notes that the place of Sone-Ve in the treatment of advanced gastric/gastro-oesophageal junction cancer will be further established when results are available from the ongoing CLARITY-Gastric02 phase III trial evaluating Sone-Ve with capecitabine, with or without rilvegostomig (the TIGIT and PD-1 bispecific antibody), as first-line treatment ( NCT07431281 ).
The findings from CLARITY-Gastric01 add to other phase III data discussed at the Congress. The G-HOPE-001 study demonstrated improved PFS with arcotatug tavatecan, an anti-CLDN18.2 antibody conjugated to exatecan (a topoisomerase 1 inhibitor) with IgG1 Fc silencing to attenuate antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity and complement-dependent cytotoxicity ( LBA77 ). In the pre-specified first interim analysis, median PFS was 5.5 months with arcotatug tavatecan and 2.9 months with treatment of the investigator’s choice (HR 0.47; 95% CI 0.34–0.65; p<0.0001) in 408 patients with advanced gastric or gastro-oesophageal junction adenocarcinoma who had received two to four prior regimens and had CLDN18.2 immunohistochemistry membrane staining intensity ≥2+ in ≥75% of tumour cells. “Notably, the two trials used substantially different CLDN18.2 expression thresholds , which should be considered when interpreting and comparing their results,” notes Al-Batran. In the G-HOPE-001 trial , median OS was 9.9 months with arcotatug tavatecan versus 7.4 months in the control group (HR 0.63; 95% CI 0.45–0.89), with formal statistical analysis expected at the pre-specified second interim analysis. “These preliminary data are promising, demonstrating a significant improvement in PFS with a manageable safety profile. However, the OS data remain immature , and longer follow-up and the planned formal OS analysis are needed to establish whether this translates into a meaningful survival benefit,” concludes Al-Batran. A bispecific antibody targeting CLDN18.2 and CD3 – ASP2138 – has just entered phase III development ( NCT07673887 ) and may provide added competition.

title: Divarasib outperforms approved KRAS G12C inhibitors in NSCLC
content:
Significant survival benefits were observed with this novel agent in the second-line setting
Results from the global Krascendo 1 trial , presented at today’s Presidential Symposium at the ESMO Congress 2026 (Madrid, 23–27 October), show that improved progression-free survival (PFS), overall survival (OS) and objective response rate (ORR) can be achieved with the KRAS G12C inhibitor divarasib , compared with two approved inhibitors, sotorasib and adagrasib, in previously treated locally advanced or metastatic KRAS G12C-mutated non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) ( LBA5 ). “Despite the early excitement surrounding sotorasib and then adagrasib, their efficacy is only limited and an OS benefit against chemotherapy has not been demonstrated ( Lancet. 2023;401:733–746 ; Lancet. 2025;406:615–626 ),” says Prof. Benjamin Besse from Institut Gustave Roussy, Villejuif, France. “Results from Krascendo 1 trial indicate that the higher potency of divarasib could translate into a new standard of care.”
The phase III trial involved 338 patients who had received 1–3 lines of prior systemic therapy , including platinum-based chemotherapy, a PD-(L)1 inhibitor and potentially, docetaxel. In the control group, 91% received sotorasib and 9% received adagrasib.
Divarasib met its primary endpoint of significantly improved PFS assessed by blinded independent central review compared with control (either sotorasib or adagrasib) (median PFS: 9.8 months versus 5.7 months; hazard ratio [HR] 0.58; 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.44–0.76; p<0.0001), after a median follow-up of 14.3 months. Of note, OS was also significantly prolonged, with median duration of 17.7 months with divarasib versus 12.0 months with control (HR 0.56; 95% CI 0.41–0.78; p=0.0005). Divarasib demonstrated a 25.8% improvement in confirmed ORR versus control. “Only 4% of patients had primary resistance, i.e., progressive disease with divarasib, which is very encouraging,” adds Besse.
Almost all patients (99%) received a checkpoint inhibitor in the first line. Regarding toxicity , Besse notes that “divarasib may be more ‘immunotherapy friendly’ than sotorasib,” which can lead to hepatoxicity after immunotherapy. There were fewer grade 3–4 treatment-related adverse events (TRAEs) with divarasib than with control (24.6% versus 34.5%). Rates of hepatotoxicity were lower with divarasib than with control (e.g., grade 3–4 alkaline phosphatase increase: 0.6% versus 4.1%), although gastrointestinal toxicity was higher with divarasib (e.g., grade 3–4 diarrhoea: 9.0% versus 2.9%). While median treatment duration was more than twice as long with divarasib versus control (11.3 months versus 5.0 months), half as many patients had TRAEs leading to treatment discontinuation (4.8% versus 11.7%).
With such impressive results in the second-line setting, combining divarasib with immunotherapy may have an important role as first-line treatment. Indeed, the Krascendo 2 trial of divarasib plus pembrolizumab versus pembrolizumab plus chemotherapy in treatment-naive advanced/metastatic KRAS G12C-mutated NSCLC is currently enrolling ( NCT06793215 ) based on results from cohorts in the Krascendo 170 phase Ib/II trial ( J Clin Oncol. 2026;44(16_Suppl.):8510). Whether chemotherapy should also be included is another potentially interesting area of study.
A large number of agents are in development, including KRAS G12C (OFF) inhibitors, KRAS G12C (ON) inhibitors, pan-RAS inhibitors and KRAS degraders, and “toxicity may be a key differentiating factor,” according to Besse. “Sotorasib or adagrasib are still only available in a small number of countries and improving drug access will be crucial for any new RAS-targeting agent to ensure that patients benefit from the pharmacological advances.”

title: Sacituzumab tirumotecan plus pembrolizumab significantly prolongs progression-free survival in advanced non-small cell lung cancer
content:
Compared to standard of care, the addition of the antibody–drug conjugate to immunotherapy was effective in PD-L1-negative patients where outcomes are usually suboptimal
Findings from a pre-planned interim analysis of the phase III OptiTROP-Lung06 study suggest that the antibody–drug conjugate (ADC) could reshape the first-line treatment landscape of non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). A 51% reduction in the risk of progression or death was demonstrated with the addition of the trophoblast cell surface antigen 2 (TROP2)-directed ADC sacituzumab tirumotecan (sac-TMT) to first-line pembrolizumab immunotherapy compared with standard of care (SOC) chemotherapy plus pembrolizumab (median progression-free survival [PFS] 15.0 months versus 5.7 months; hazard ratio [HR] 0.49; 95% confidence interval 0.36–0.65; p<0.0001) at a median follow-up of 9.7 months ( LBA66 ). The analysis of PFS , the primary endpoint of the study, was presented as a Late-Breaking Abstract at the ESMO Congress 2026 (Madrid, 23–27 October). The trial included 455 patients from China who had treatment-naïve, locally advanced or metastatic non-squamous NSCLC without EGFR or ALK alterations and a PD-L1 tumour proportion score <1%.
“Pembrolizumab plus chemotherapy is the current standard first-line treatment in this setting, but outcomes remain suboptimal, especially in patients with PD-L1-negative tumours,” Dr Giannis Mountzios from Henry Dunant Hospital Center, Athens, Greece, notes. The sac-TMT plus pembrolizumab combination previously demonstrated significantly increased median PFS compared with pembrolizumab alone as first-line treatment for patients with PD-L1-positive advanced NSCLC in the OptiTROP-Lung05 study (median PFS not reached versus 5.7 months; HR 0.35; p<0.0001) ( Lancet. 2026;407:2607–2619 ).
“The dramatic PFS improvement with the addition of ADC to pembrolizumab compared with SOC represents an important milestone; it is the first time this has been demonstrated in patients with PD-L1-negative disease in a randomised phase III study,” adds Mountzios.
Overall survival (OS) data were immature at the time of analysis, but a favourable trend towards improved OS was observed in the sac-TMT plus pembrolizumab group (HR 0.58; 95% CI 0.38–0.88). Higher objective response rate (50.2% versus 47.3%) and a prolonged duration of response (median 13.6 months versus 6.8 months) were also observed in the sac-TMT group.
“While OS data are awaited, the PFS data are highly clinically relevant and have the potential to be immediately practice-changing in patients with PD-L1-negative tumours who experience poor outcomes. This is an area of high unmet need that could be addressed by combining ADCs with immunotherapy,” emphasises Mountzios.
Safety was described as manageable, consistent with the known profiles of the individual agents and with no apparent excess of interstitial lung disease or pneumonitis with sac-TMT. “ Treatment-emergent adverse events , including haematological toxicities, were actually less frequent in patients who received the ADC than in those who received chemotherapy and this is important for patients’ quality of life,” observes Mountzios. Grade ≥3 treatment-emergent adverse events were reported in 47.6% versus 60.6% of patients, respectively. Sac-TMT-associated adverse events of special interest included stomatitis, which was predominantly grade 1–2 (51.1%); grade ≥3 stomatitis occurred in 2.2% of sac-TMT-treated patients.

title: Savolitinib plus osimertinib prolongs both progression-free and overall survival in mutated NSCLC
content:
Practice-changing results from the SAFFRON study highlight the value of biomarker-directed therapy after progression on osimertinib in selected patients with EGFR -mutated, MET-overexpressed or amplified NSCLC
Practice-changing primary results from the phase III SAFFRON study were presented at today’s Presidential Symposium at the ESMO Congress 2026 (Madrid, 23–27 October), showing that the combination of the third-generation EGFR-TKI osimertinib plus savolitinib, a highly selective, CNS-penetrant MET-TKI, was associated with significant and clinically meaningful improvements in progression-free survival (PFS) and overall survival (OS) compared with platinum–pemetrexed in patients with EGFR -mutated, MET -overexpressed and/or -amplified advanced non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) with disease progression on osimertinib ( LBA6 ).
“In this setting, this is the first study to demonstrate both PFS and OS benefit from targeting MET resistance after osimertinib in patients with high MET expression or MET amplification,” comments Prof. Natasha Leighl from the Princess Margaret Cancer Centre, University of Toronto, Canada. “For appropriately selected patients with confirmed MET -high expression (3+ by immunohistochemistry) or amplification after osimertinib, the results support osimertinib plus savolitinib as a new standard of care treatment option.”
After a median follow-up of 5.6 months in the osimertinib plus savolitinib arm and 3.5 months in the platinum–pemetrexed arm, the respective median PFS by blinded independent central review – the primary endpoint – was 7.6 months versus 5.4 months (hazard ratio [HR] 0.55; 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.42–0.72; p<0.001). Overall PFS maturity was 68%.
Median OS was 17.8 months for osimertinib plus savolitinib and 12.9 months for platinum–pemetrexed (HR 0.68; 95% CI 0.50–0.91; p=0.010 with significance threshold set at p<0.03047) at a median follow-up of 14.2 months and 10.2 months in the respective treatment arms. Overall maturity for OS was 53%.
Based on the study findings, Leighl believes that “Repeating molecular testing at progression should become routine to enable precision treatment of resistance ,” rather than the current non-selective approach of treating all patients with chemotherapy or, where available, an antibody–drug conjugate-based regimen.
Of the 1373 patients enrolled in SAFFRON, 35% of patients evaluable for MET dysregulation analysis had MET overexpression and/or amplification. The study included patients with disease progression specifically on osimertinib, building on previous results from the phase III SACHI study conducted in China, which showed that the combination of osimertinib plus savolitinib prolonged PFS in patients with EGFR -mutated NSCLC and acquired MET amplification after progression on any first-line EGFR TKI ( Lancet. 2026;407:375–387 ).
Grade ≥3 treatment-related adverse events (TRAEs) occurred in 40% of patients in the osimertinib plus savolitinib arm and in 52% of patients in the platinum–pemetrexed arm with a similar incidence of serious TRAEs (14% versus 16%). The most common TRAEs in the osimertinib plus savolitinib arm were peripheral oedema (42%), nausea (21%), increased creatine kinase (20%), and paronychia (20%).
Osimertinib plus savolitinib offers patients convenience and a less invasive regimen. “It provides patients with a much-needed oral option to tackle progressive disease,” says Leighl, adding, “ Access to repeat molecular testing , including validated MET testing, regulatory approval and drug affordability are now essential to enable access for patients.”

四川科伦博泰生物医药股份有限公司("科伦博泰"或"公司"，6990.HK)宣布，在西班牙马德里举行的2026年欧洲肿瘤内科学会(ESMO)大会上，同济大学附属东方医院周彩存教授以口头报告形式公布了芦康沙妥珠单抗(sac-TMT，亦称SKB264/MK-2870)(佳泰莱®)III期OptiTROP-Lung06研究结果(LBA66；优选口头报告(Proffered paper)|转移性NSCLC)。

安全性方面，芦康沙妥珠单抗(sac-TMT)联合帕博利珠单抗的安全性特征与各单药已知的安全性特征总体一致，未观察到新的安全性信号。与含铂双药化疗联合帕博利珠单抗组相比，芦康沙妥珠单抗(sac-TMT)联合治疗组≥3级治疗期间出现的不良事件(TEAE)发生率较低；导致剂量降低或永久停药的TEAE发生率也较低。两组间质性肺病/肺炎发生率相似。
同济大学附属东方医院周彩存教授表示："随着OptiTROP-Lung06研究结果的读出，我们进一步看到了芦康沙妥珠单抗(sac-TMT)联合帕博利珠单抗方案在PD-L1阴性、EGFR/ALK阴性晚期非鳞状NSCLC一线治疗中的临床价值。结合此前2026年ASCO大会公布的OptiTROP-Lung05研究成果，该联合方案在不同PD-L1表达状态的无驱动基因NSCLC患者中均显示出PFS获益，为其一线治疗提供了新的III期研究证据。"
OptiTROP-Lung06研究
OptiTROP-Lung06(NCT06711900)是一项随机、多中心、开放标签III期研究，共纳入455例患者，按1:1比例随机接受芦康沙妥珠单抗(sac-TMT)联合帕博利珠单抗或含铂双药化疗(培美曲塞联合顺铂或卡铂)联合帕博利珠单抗治疗。主要终点为BICR评估的PFS，次要终点包括OS等。截至数据截止日期(2026年6月9日)，中位随访时间为9.7个月。这是全球首个ADC联合免疫检查点抑制剂在一线治疗驱动基因阴性、PD-L1阴性非鳞状NSCLC上达到主要终点的III期临床研究。

关于芦康沙妥珠单抗(sac-TMT)(佳泰莱®)
作为公司的核心产品，芦康沙妥珠单抗(sac-TMT)是一款公司拥有自主知识产权的新型TROP2 ADC，针对NSCLC、乳腺癌(BC)、胃癌(GC)、妇科肿瘤及泌尿生殖系统肿瘤等晚期实体瘤。芦康沙妥珠单抗(sac-TMT)采用独特双功能连接子开发而成。该连接子一方面通过与抗TROP2单克隆抗体沙妥珠单抗形成不可逆结合，另一方面在溶酶体中可从贝洛替康衍生物拓扑异构酶I抑制剂有效载荷(KL610023)pH敏感裂解，从而最大限度将有效载荷递送至肿瘤细胞，药物抗体比(DAR)达到7.4。芦康沙妥珠单抗(sac-TMT)通过重组抗TROP2人源化单克隆抗体特异性识别肿瘤细胞表面的TROP2，其后被肿瘤细胞内吞并于细胞内释放有效载荷KL610023。KL610023可诱导肿瘤细胞DNA损伤，进而导致细胞周期阻滞及细胞凋亡。此外，其亦于肿瘤微环境中释放KL610023。鉴于KL610023具有细胞膜渗透性，其可实现旁观者效应，即杀死邻近的肿瘤细胞。
于2022年5月，公司授予默沙东(美国新泽西州罗威市默克公司的商号)在大中华区(包括中国内地、香港、澳门及台湾)以外的所有地区开发、使用、制造及商业化芦康沙妥珠单抗(sac-TMT)的独家权利。
截至目前，芦康沙妥珠单抗(sac-TMT)的4项适应症已于中国获批上市，分别用于：1)既往至少接受过2种系统治疗(其中至少1种治疗针对晚期或转移性阶段)的不可切除的局部晚期或转移性三阴性乳腺癌(TNBC)；2)EGFR-酪氨酸激酶抑制剂(TKI)和含铂化疗治疗后进展的EGFR基因突变阳性的局部晚期或转移性非鳞状NSCLC；3)经EGFR-TKI治疗后进展的EGFR基因突变阳性的局部晚期或转移性非鳞状NSCLC；4)既往接受过内分泌治疗且在晚期疾病阶段接受过至少一线化疗的不可切除或转移性的激素受体阳性(HR+)且人类表皮生长因子受体2阴性(HER2-) (免疫组织化学(IHC) 0、IHC 1+或IHC 2+/原位杂交(ISH)-) BC；其中前2项适应症已经被纳入医保范围，将为更多乳腺癌和非小细胞肺癌患者带来临床获益。此外，芦康沙妥珠单抗(sac-TMT)已获NMPA授予6项突破性疗法认定。
芦康沙妥珠单抗(sac-TMT)是全球首个在肺癌适应症获批上市的TROP2 ADC药物。芦康沙妥珠单抗(sac-TMT)的两项新增适应症上市申请已获NMPA受理，分别用于：1)联合帕博利珠单抗一线治疗PD-L1 TPS≥1%的EGFR基因突变阴性和ALK阴性的局部晚期或转移性NSCLC；2)PD-L1综合阳性评分(CPS)<10或早期阶段接受过PD-1/PD-L1抑制剂的复发或转移性TNBC的一线治疗，以上两项申请均被纳入优先审评审批程序。目前，公司已在中国开展9项注册性临床研究。默沙东已启动18项正在进行的芦康沙妥珠单抗(sac-TMT)作为单药疗法或联合帕博利珠单抗或其他抗癌药物用于多种类型癌症的全球性III期临床研究(这些研究由默沙东申办并主导)。

title: Omega-3 EPA Linked to Longer Survival After Surgery for Colorectal Cancer Liver Metastases
content:
In the phase 3 EMT2 trial, five-year overall survival was 62% with EPA versus 45% with placebo after surgery for colorectal cancer liver metastases.
EPA did not significantly improve progression-free survival, the trial's primary endpoint.
The findings suggest a possible role for EPA in care around and after liver surgery, but further trials are needed before routine use.
Lugano/Madrid – Patients assigned to receive high-dose eicosapentaenoic acid (EPA), an omega-3 fatty acid, before and after surgery for colorectal cancer liver metastases had longer overall survival than those assigned to receive placebo, according to results of the phase 3 EMT2 trial presented at the ESMO Congress 2026 . (1)
Surgery to remove colorectal cancer that has spread to the liver offers the possibility of long-term survival, but recurrence remains common. Preclinical and observational studies have suggested that EPA may have activity against colorectal cancer, while an earlier phase 2 trial indicated a possible survival benefit. (2)
The randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled EMT2 trial enrolled 418 patients scheduled for liver resection with curative intent at 13 UK hepatobiliary surgery centres. Patients were assigned to 4g daily of EPA, as high-purity prescription icosapent ethyl, or mineral oil placebo. Treatment began at least one day before surgery and was planned to continue for two to four years, even after cancer progression. Other cancer treatments were broadly comparable, with 20% in each group receiving adjuvant chemotherapy.
Estimated five-year overall survival, the trial’s key secondary endpoint, was 62.0% with EPA versus 45.1% with placebo. EPA was associated with a 32% lower hazard of death (hazard ratio [HR] 0.68; 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.48–0.96; p=0.03). Median overall survival had not been reached with EPA versus 59.0 months with placebo. The survival benefit was consistent in the per-protocol analysis (HR 0.60; 95% CI 0.36–0.99). It also remained consistent after adjustment for diabetes, which was more common at baseline in the EPA group (16% versus 8%), and in other sensitivity analyses. However, median progression-free survival (PFS) was similar in the two groups (13.5 versus 12.9 months; HR 0.89; 95% CI 0.70–1.13; p=0.33).
EPA was well tolerated, with no excess adverse events, bleeding or atrial fibrillation compared with placebo, and no negative impact on quality of life.
“The overall survival benefit seen with EPA in EMT2, if confirmed in other studies, is clinically meaningful for the group of patients who have had surgery for bowel cancer spread to the liver and in whom the cancer frequently comes back,” said lead author Professor Mark Hull, Leeds Institute of Medical Research, University of Leeds, UK. “This is particularly the case as EPA is well-tolerated and safe, even when other cancer treatments are needed.”
Hull suggested the survival benefit might reflect effects on the body’s response to cancer, including cachexia, which can involve weight loss, reduced appetite and fatigue. “Longer overall survival but no significant improvement in progression-free survival has also been seen in trials of cancer immunotherapy, and more research is needed to work out whether EPA works by improving the body’s immune response to cancer,” he said.
“The results are definitely intriguing, from both a biological and a clinical point of view,” said Dr Chiara Cremolini, University of Pisa, Italy, who was not involved in the study. “The lack of concordance between progression-free survival and overall survival results requires careful interpretation.” She noted that PFS is a less established indicator of overall survival after surgery for liver metastases than after surgery for early-stage bowel cancer, and that additional data would help, including the treatments patients received after their cancer came back and the pattern of spread at the time of progression.
“Confirmatory results are likely needed before incorporating this treatment option into daily clinical practice,” said Cremolini, noting that patients having surgery for liver metastases vary widely in the biological and molecular characteristics of their cancer and in their previous treatment, which future trials could take into account. “Acknowledging the difficulty of conducting clinical trials, and especially academic research, in this setting, the authors should be highly congratulated for their successful effort,” she concluded.

title: Advanced renal cancer: data support the use of belzutifan in later lines, but not first line
content:
Results from LITESPARK-012 and LITESPARK-011 open the discussion on the role of the HIF-2α inhibitor in the treatment pathway
Frontline triplet therapy has been proposed as an approach to improve outcomes in advanced clear-cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC). As more agents are approved, there is much interest in determining whether they could be moved into the first-line setting to improve cure rates. This is the case with belzutifan, a first-in-class hypoxia-inducible factor 2-alpha (HIF-2α) inhibitor, which is well tolerated as a single agent and is approved after anti-PD-(L)1 therapy and after VEGFR TKI therapy in advanced RCC ( Nat Med. 2021;27:802–805 ; Ther Adv Med Oncol. 2025;17:17588359251317846 ). However, key findings presented in a Proffered Paper Session at the ESMO Congress 2026 (Madrid, 23–27 October), highlight that when belzutifan was added to pembrolizumab plus lenvatinib – the standard of care (SOC) in the first-line setting – survival was not improved and the triplet was associated with drug discontinuations ( Abstract 3586O , key results in the box below).
The phase III LITESPARK-012 study investigated the addition of either belzutifan or MK-1308A (anti-CTLA-4 quavonlimab plus pembrolizumab co-formulation) to SOC in 1,688 patients with previously untreated advanced ccRCC. At a median follow-up of 43.6 months, median progression-free survival (PFS) was 20.8 months, 20.7 months and 23.7 months in the belzutifan, MK-1308A and SOC arms, respectively. Median overall survival (OS) was 52.0 months, not reached (NR) and NR. The objective response rate (ORR) was 69.1%, 69.0% and 76.3%.
“All of the combinations do well, but patients receiving the belzutifan and MK-1308A combinations experienced higher rates of toxicity and higher discontinuation rates of pembrolizumab, MK-1308A and lenvatinib than those in the SOC arm,” highlights Dr Naomi Balzer-Haas from Hospital of the University of Pennsylvania, Philadelphia, PA, USA, “So whether this agent may have a role in first-line therapy for advanced disease is, at the moment, uncertain.” Grade ≥3 treatment-related adverse events (TRAEs) were reported in 77.5%, 78.3% and 69.1% of patients and AEs resulted in discontinuation of any drug in 51.6%, 51.4% and 36.2% of patients, respectively. The authors suggest this may have limited drug exposure and potentially impacted efficacy.
Belzutifan combined with lenvatinib is showing greater promise in patients with advanced ccRCC who previously progressed on first- or second-line anti-PD-(L)1 therapy, as final analysis data from the phase III LITESPARK-011 study demonstrate ( Abstract 3587O , key results in the box below). As previously reported, at a median follow-up of 38.8 months, belzutifan combined with lenvatinib maintained the statistically significant improvements in PFS and ORR versus cabozantinib previously reported at earlier interim analyses ( Lancet. 2026;408:808–820 ). As presented in Madrid, median PFS was 14.8 months versus 10.8 months (HR 0.74, 95% CI 0.62–0.88), ORR was 53.1% versus 40.1% (p=0.0002) and the median duration of response was 22.0 months versus 11.9 months in 747 patients with advanced ccRCC who previously progressed on first- or second-line anti–PD-(L)1 therapy. Also, a trend towards improved OS was observed with belzutifan plus lenvatinib versus cabozantinib (median 33.7 months versus 28.6 months; HR 0.85; 95% CI 0.70–1.03; p=0.04689 [pre-specified boundary 0.0223]). Grade ≥3 TRAEs occurred at a slightly higher rate in the combination arm than with cabozantinib (73.2% versus 66.6%).
“The lack of statistical significance for OS is disappointing, and it may have been confounded by the subsequent use of the study agents across different lines of therapy, making it difficult to show a survival benefit,” suggests Balzer-Haas. Patients randomised to receive belzutifan plus lenvatinib frequently received subsequent cabozantinib (37.2%). Patients randomised to cabozantinib went on to receive subsequent therapies including lenvatinib with/without everolimus (17.6%), cabozantinib again (12.2%) and belzutifan (7.4%). “Overall, the data continue to support the use of belzutifan plus lenvatinib following anti-PD-(L)1 therapy,” she adds. “For patients who receive ipilimumab and nivolumab as first-line treatment, belzutifan plus lenvatinib will likely be used in the second-line setting. Similarly, if cabozantinib plus nivolumab or axitinib plus pembrolizumab are used as a first-line combination, lenvatinib plus belzutifan may be used on disease progression.”
Ongoing trials are comparing belzutifan combinations, such as belzutifan plus the TKI, zanzalintinib, versus cabozantinib in the phase III LITESPARK-033 trial in advanced, recurrent ccRCC after adjuvant anti-PD-(L)1 therapy ( J Clin Oncol. 2026;44(Suppl 16):TPS4633 ). The investigational HIF-2α inhibitor, casdatifan is also showing encouraging activity in patients with refractory metastatic ccRCC ( Nature. 2026;656:734–741 ) and is being studied in combination with cabozantinib in patients with advanced ccRCC after progression on anti-PD-(L)1 therapy in the ongoing phase III PEAK-1 study ( NCT07011719 ). “Each of these combinations appears to be well tolerated so they may have a role to play in the future,” remarks Balzer-Haas.

title: ROBOT-2随机III期试验证实机器人食管癌切除术淋巴结清扫更彻底且安全性相当【AI生成】
content:
《JAMA Surgery》发表荷兰、德国、瑞士四中心联合开展的ROBOT-2随机III期优效性试验结果。该研究对比机器人辅助微创食管切除术（RAMIE）与常规胸腹腔镜微创食管切除术（MIE）治疗可切除食管及食管胃交界部腺癌的疗效。在消除学习曲线干扰并统一病理处理标准的前提下，RAMIE组中位淋巴结清扫数显著多于MIE组（36枚 vs 32枚，P=.005），但两组在R0切除率、术后并发症发生率（53.5% vs 47.5%）、90天死亡率及12个月总生存率方面均无统计学差异。研究结论支持RAMIE在提高手术彻底性方面的优势，且未增加安全风险，为机器人食管切除术作为标准术式提供了高级别循证医学证据。

title: Adding chemotherapy to pembrolizumab leads to progression-free survival benefit in NSCLC
content:
Phase III results from the PERSEE study are practice-confirming, suggesting an advantage for the combination as first-line therapy in patients with PD-L1 ≥50% advanced tumours
Results from the open-label, phase III PERSEE trial were presented at the ESMO Congress 2026 (Madrid, 23–27 October) and showed a significant progression-free survival (PFS) benefit by blinded central review – the primary endpoint – for platinum-based chemotherapy plus pembrolizumab versus pembrolizumab monotherapy in the first-line treatment of advanced non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) ( Abstract 2614O ). “A chemotherapy-sparing strategy is often the treatment of choice for patients with NSCLC and PD-L1 ≥50%, but these findings, showing a 44% reduction in the risk of disease progression or death, cast doubt on the use of immunotherapy alone in these patients,” states Prof. Alfredo Addeo from Geneva University Hospitals, Switzerland, commenting on the PFS of 16.1 months reported in the combination therapy group compared with 6.9 months achieved with the monotherapy. The PFS benefit was observed across all subgroups and regardless of PD-L1 expression level.
In the trial, which involved 321 patients, PFS data in the pembrolizumab arm appeared lower than that reported in previous research, such as 10.3 months in the phase III KEYNOTE-024 trial ( N Engl J Med. 2016;375:1823–1833 ), thus suggesting that at least for the patients selected in this trial, pembrolizumab monotherapy did not perform as well as expected. Addeo adds: “Although cross-trial comparisons should always be interpreted with caution, the median PFS of 6.9 months observed with pembrolizumab monotherapy in PERSEE is disappointing compared with the 10.3 months reported in the pivotal KEYNOTE-024 trial in the same clinical setting. This raises the question of whether differences in baseline patient characteristics or other prognostic factors may have contributed to the relatively poor performance of the pembrolizumab-only arm in PERSEE. Understanding these differences will be important when interpreting the magnitude of benefit observed with the addition of chemotherapy.”
In PERSEE, the median overall survival (OS) was 50.2 months versus 29.9 months (hazard ratio 0.77), and the objective response rate (ORR) was 77.5% versus 50.3% for chemotherapy–pembrolizumab versus pembrolizumab monotherapy. “While the OS result is not statistically significant (as the trial was not powered to demonstrated an OS difference), the survival benefit is substantial with combination therapy,” notes Addeo. The PERSEE results, he says, “are practice-confirming rather than practice-changing and, in some countries, may make it easier to access chemotherapy for these patients.” Addeo suggests certain subgroups would benefit most from the chemotherapy–pembrolizumab combination. “Patients with heavily symptomatic disease or high disease burden in whom response to first-line treatment is key might do better with the combination – provided they can tolerate the known side effects of chemotherapy. On the other hand, patients with low disease burden, asymptomatic disease or those with very high PD-L1 status (>80%) may not require chemotherapy.”
Regarding the toxicity profile of the combination therapy, grade ≥3 treatment-related adverse events were reported in 54.4% of patients in the chemotherapy–pembrolizumab arm and in 19.5% of patients in the pembrolizumab monotherapy arm.
The PERSEE trial shares a similar design and patient population to the recently presented phase III KEYNOTE-D46/EVOKE-03 trial , which showed that the combination of the antibody–drug conjugate (ADC) sacituzumab govitecan plus pembrolizumab did not achieve a statistically significant improvement in PFS versus pembrolizumab monotherapy. “Interestingly, outcomes from the 2 studies were very different,” Addeo concludes, “ADCs are considered to be newer and more potent; however, they may not bring a clinical benefit. These recent findings indicate that a chemotherapy payload in an ADC may not be sufficient and that some patients may still require the ‘old-fashioned’ platinum-based chemotherapy.”

title: Promising results support wider development of ADCs in less common cancers
content:
Demonstrations of activity, supported by technological advances in drug design and agnostic approvals, may expand options for patients with few established treatment options
Results from three trials presented at the ESMO Congress 2026 (Madrid, 23–27 October) highlight how the scene is now set for antibody–drug conjugates (ADCs) to be explored beyond the most common cancers. “Expanding the range of targetable antigens, together with advances in ADC design and a better understanding of the mechanisms of action such as the bystander effect, have brought opportunities to test this drug class in less frequent cancers and cancer conditions,” confirms Dr Fernanda Mosele , Gustave Roussy, Villejuif, France. “Importantly, there is proof of concept that tumour agnostic approvals are possible with the authorisation of trastuzumab deruxtecan as a tumour-agnostic HER2-directed therapy in HER2-positive solid tumours. In addition, basket trial designs and regulatory framework evolvement are helping to facilitate targeted testing where patient populations are small.”
At the Congress, significant overall response rate (ORR) data were reported in 431 patients with heavily pre-treated recurrent/metastatic nasopharyngeal carcinoma, a setting where there are no established third-line therapies ( LBA43 , key results in the box below). The phase III TAISHAN-301 trial with tambotatug pelitecan (Tam-Peli), an ADC that targets B7-H3, met one of its primary endpoints: ORR was 50.8% versus 25.8% with treatment of physician’s choice (odds ratio 2.9; 95% confidence interval 1.7–5.0; p<0.0001). The disease control rate (DCR) was 93.7% and 75.8% with Tam-Peli versus treatment of physician’s choice, respectively, and the median duration of response (DOR) was 7.9 months and 6.4 months.
“These findings confirm that targeting an immune checkpoint modulator with an ADC represents a very novel and effective approach. They further reinforce the positive results observed with Tam-Peli in small cell lung cancer ( N Engl J Med. 2026 Sep 12. doi: 10.1056/NEJMoa2610229 ), while extending the benefit to a broader patient population and highlight its potential applicability across multiple tumour types ,” explains Mosele. Mature data are awaited for the other primary endpoint, overall survival (OS), and for progression-free survival (PFS). The safety profile was manageable, with no new safety concerns. Grade ≥3 treatment-related adverse events (TRAEs) were reported in 49.3% of patients with Tam-Peli versus 51.7% of patients with treatment of physician’s choice, most commonly neutropenia in both groups. “Since the TAISHAN-301 trial was conducted in China, it will be key to see a global trial in nasopharyngeal carcinoma to assess whether Tam-Peli remains effective across populations with different ethnic backgrounds and epidemiological characteristics,” she adds.
Positive results were also presented for the HER3-targeting ADC, patritumab deruxtecan (HER3-DXd), in cohorts of patients with central nervous system (CNS) metastases ( Abstract 690O , key results in the box below). In the phase II TUXEDO-3 trial , at extended follow-up, median OS reached 7.9 months in 21 patients with active brain metastases and metastatic breast cancer, 6.7 months in 20 patients with active brain metastases and non-small cell lung cancer, and 10.5 months in 20 patients with leptomeningeal disease from any solid malignancy. Intracranial PFS was 4.0 months, 5.7 months and 3.9 months, respectively. Neurological symptoms, quality of life and neurocognitive function remained stable or improved during treatment.
“The therapeutic value of HER3-DXd in this trial reinforces the role of ADCs as a promising treatment approach for patients with secondary CNS disease who have been underrepresented previously and present a poor outcome. Trastuzumab deruxtecan has demonstrated intracranial responses in breast cancer of ~50% ( ESMO Open. 2024;9:103699 ; Nat Med. 2024;30:3717–3727 ), suggesting that this is a class effect of modern topoisomerase 1 inhibitor ADCs rather than a drug-specific property,” suggests Mosele. She notes that the use of Response Assessment in Neuro-Oncology for Brain Metastases (RANO-BM) outcome criteria in the trial establishes an important framework for the evaluation of ADCs in CNS disease, while underscoring the need for more dedicated trials specifically designed to evaluate intracranial efficacy. “Understanding the mechanisms underlying CNS activity – including the role of the free payload – and the HER3-DXd pharmacokinetics in the CNS compartment – are also very important,” she adds.
Finally, an ORR of 45.5% was observed in the phase I CATALINA-1 trial of ixotatug vedotin (Ixo-V), a first-in-class IgG1-vc-MMAE claudin-6 (CLDN6) ADC, in 11 patients with heavily pre-treated CLDN6-positive germ cell tumours ( Abstract 1210RO , key results in the box below). The DCR was 72.7% and the median DOR was 4.5 months. Three of 6 patients who received prior autologous stem cell transplantation had confirmed responses with Ixo-V. Peripheral sensory neuropathy was the most common adverse event leading to dose delay or reduction in 5 patients. One patient discontinued due to TRAEs.
“The ORR with Ixo-V exceeds what is typically achieved with salvage chemotherapy in this setting so these early results in heavily pre-treated patients are encouraging,” notes Mosele. Positive preliminary results with Ixo-V have previously been shown in solid tumours, including germ cell tumours and ovarian cancer, tumour types where CLDN6 is overexpressed, with an ORR of ~30–40% ( ESMO Open 2026;11(Suppl 6):140P ; Ann Oncol. 2024;35(suppl 2):S551 ; Int J Gynecol Cancer. 2024;34(Suppl 3):A56 ).
Adding to these encouraging findings, extensive biomarker analyses will help define which patients benefit most from each ADC. “The use of new technologies, such as digital pathology , may help better predict response than conventional immunohistochemistry, as previously shown ( Cancer Cell. 2026;44:1147–1159.e6 ),” concludes Mosele. “The development and approval of companion diagnostic tests may be a challenge if treatments are only active in a small patient population, but the experience gained in more common cancers and in agnostic pathways may help to bring ADCs to patients with less common cancers.”

title: Are multispecific agents shaping the future of cancer research?
content:
Different promising strategies emerge from three early-phase trials, showing good tolerability in colorectal cancer and clear cell renal cell carcinoma
Advances in bioengineering have enabled the design of molecules targeting the tumour microenvironment (TME) and the development of multiple strategies to boost the antitumour response, such as bispecific and trispecific antibodies , and T-cell engagers (TCEs) ( J Immunother Cancer. 2025;13:e011761 ; Br J Cancer. 2025;133:1241–1249 ; iScience. 2025;28:114203 ). Although research in this area can face a number of possible hurdles , it continues to gain momentum in solid cancers, providing valuable insights into strategies for addressing multiple tumour targets, either simultaneously or sequentially.
A well-tolerated potential candidate for further research in microsatellite stable (MSS) colorectal cancer (CRC) is the TGF-β receptor 2 (TGFβR2)- and PD-1-targeting bispecific antibody, INCA33890, due to the low toxicity shown in a phase I study presented at ESMO Congress 2026 (Madrid, 23–27 October) ( Abstract 1954RO , key results in the box below). The agent was investigated in combination with standard of care therapies and, depending on the chosen combination, was associated with grade ≥3 treatment-emergent adverse events (TEAEs) of neutropenia and neutrophil count decrease (0–66.7%) – leading to chemotherapy dose reductions in 0–67.4% of patients – and stomatitis (0–16.7%) in 94 patients, depending on the chemotherapy regimen partner. “The 10.3–16.7% incidence of grade ≥3 immune-related AEs is below what we might usually expect with a PD-1 inhibitor,” notes Prof. Alessandra Curioni-Fontecedro from the University of Fribourg and Cantonal Hospital Fribourg, Switzerland. In the study, there were no INCA33890-related dose-limiting toxicities and immune-related AEs were reported in 33.0–83.3% of patients across the treatment arms, most commonly diarrhoea, pruritus and stomatitis (16.7–50.0%), with 0–16.7% having grade ≥3 events. Reported objective response rates (ORRs) were 71.4% for first-line INCA33890 plus FOLFOX and bevacizumab in efficacy-evaluable patients (n=42), including 82.8% in 29 patients with liver metastases, 28.2% for INCA33890 plus bevacizumab in the +3-line (L) setting (n=39), and 50.0% for INCA33890 plus FOLFIRI and bevacizumab in the +2L setting (n=6). The disease control rate (DCR) in these cohorts ranged from 46.2–100%.
“ Metastatic CRC (mCRC) is considered to be unresponsive to immunotherapy but, due to its aggressiveness and the paucity of available treatment options, using these agents seems like a logical step to help reverse the immunosuppressive TME by targeting immunosuppressive cells, blocking inhibitory metabolic pathways and in particular, targeting VEGF , which is crucial for the development of metastasis in this disease,” says Curioni-Fontecedro. “These results point to a synergistic mechanism of action between INCA33890 and the VEGF-targeting bevacizumab, which may represent a potential strategy for the future treatment of mCRC.”
A high DCR was also observed with a XmAb819 monotherapy, a first-in-class T-cell engaging dual-antigen antibody targeting the ENPP3 protein in patients with advanced clear cell renal cell carcinoma in a second phase I study ( Abstract 3588O , key results in the box below). According to Curioni-Fontecedro, “This could represent an important treatment option in highly symptomatic patients who have no available alternative therapies.” As discussed at the Congress, among 66 efficacy-evaluable patients who received XmAb819, the ORR was 30.0% at target dose 100 μg/kg, 44.0% at target dose 200 μg/kg and 45.5% at target dose 400 μg/kg, while DCRs ranged from 64.0–86.7%, with ORR and DCR consistent in patients who had received ≥2 prior VEGFR-TKIs (n=42; 45.2%, 85.7%) or had prior HIF2α inhibitor exposure (n=23; 34.8, 78.3%). Grade ≥3 treatment-related AEs (TRAEs) occurred in 72.1% of patients, leading to treatment discontinuation in 5.9%. Curioni-Fontecedro thinks that the discontinuation rate reported is not unexpected, as this is a heavily pre-treated population with likely accumulated side effects from previous treatments.
Safety seems not to be a major concern in the continued development of CS2009, a first-in-class trispecific antibody targeting PD-1, VEGF and CTLA-4, as data from a third Congress presentation suggests ( Abstract 1953RO , key results in the box below). In a phase I/II study, grade ≥3 TEAEs possibly related to anti-VEGF treatment occurred in 2 (8.7%) previously treated patients with mCRC who received CS2009 monotherapy in the phase I part of the study (n=23), and in 1 (4.3%) patient receiving 1L CS2009 plus XELOX in the phase II part of the study (n=23). Common TEAEs possibly related to anti-VEGF treatment in previously treated patients were proteinuria (17.4%), epistaxis (8.7%) and urinary occult blood positive (8.7%; all grade 1–2), while in treatment-naïve patients, these events occurred in 8.7%, 0% and 4.3% of patients, respectively, which were all grade 1–2, with 1 (4.3%) of grade ≥3 proteinuria. Any-grade immune-related events were reported in 26.1% of previously treated patients and in 39.1% of treatment-naïve patients. Among 15 efficacy-evaluable phase I patients, the ORR was 20.0%, including 3 partial responses, and the DCR was 93.3%, while among 22 efficacy-evaluable phase II patients, the ORR was 59.1% and the DCR was 100%.
While research in multispecific agents is likely to increase the treatment options currently available for different tumour types, it also poses a challenge in terms of selecting the optimal biomarker for each patient. “Understanding a patient’s specific tumour and TME prior to therapy could help determine which biomarker to use and consequently, which treatment to select. Another major issue is to determine the optimal sequence of targeted treatments , particularly when several novel therapies with different targets are developed simultaneously,” concludes Curioni-Fontecedro.

title: Cell：肠道菌代谢物决定 CAR-T细胞成败！戊酸助阵、吲哚拖后腿，代谢风险评分可预测疗效
content:
Cell：肠道菌代谢物决定 CAR-T细胞成败！戊酸助阵、吲哚拖后腿，代谢风险评分可预测疗效
来源：生物谷原创 2026-10-21 10:47
这项研究为肠道微生物组在CAR-T细胞疗法中的作用提供了新视角。
免疫疗法，尤其是 CAR-T细胞疗法，近年来从根本上改变了癌症治疗，特别是某些形式的白血病和淋巴瘤。然而，并非所有肿瘤都同样反应良好，其原因仍未被完全理解。莱布尼茨免疫治疗研究所合作组 Innate Immune Sensing in Cancer and Transplantation 的一项新多中心研究现在表明，决定CAR-T细胞疗法成功的不仅是肠道微生物群的组成，而尤其是其代谢产物。
正如发表在 Cell 期刊上所述，某些微生物代谢物可以增强或抑制CAR-T细胞功能，对治疗结局产生重大影响。它们还为基于微生物组的疗法和旨在癌症治疗期间支持肠道微生物组的饮食策略提供了起点。
这项研究以来自 Munich (LMU)、Heidelberg 和 Regensburg 的 3 所德国大学医院的 129 名患者的观察性队列为中心。使用先进的微生物组和代谢组分析，研究团队鉴定了与 CAR-T细胞疗法应答或失败相关的肠道微生物组代谢物。
然后在小鼠模型和使用人类CAR-T细胞的临床前模型中测试了这些代谢物。这使研究人员能够分析它们对CAR-T细胞活性、代谢和疗效的直接影响，并首次更详细地阐明潜在生物学机制。
“我们的结果表明，单个微生物代谢物可以产生非常不同的影响，因此如果未来要利用肠道微生物组来预测或改善治疗成功，就需要具体考虑它们，”Hendrik Poeck 说。
特别值得注意的是短链脂肪酸戊酸：治疗前水平低与疾病进展风险更高相关，而治疗性给药改善了人类和小鼠模型中的CAR-T细胞功能。
相比之下，吲哚代谢物如吲哚-3-甲醛（Indole-3-carboxaldehyde） 和‌吲哚-3-乙酸‌（indole-3-acetic acid ） 水平升高与不利结局相关；这些代谢物在人类和小鼠模型中都降低了CAR-T细胞疗效。异戊酸，一种支链脂肪酸，被证明更复杂：它在某些方面改善了CAR-T细胞功能，但也与一种此前未知的促肿瘤作用相关。
微生物组复杂性：对免疫系统和肿瘤都有影响
这项研究为肠道微生物组在CAR-T细胞疗法中的作用提供了新视角。直到现在，研究主要集中在细菌组成上。这项工作反而表明，微生物代谢物是影响治疗成功的关键生物学角色。研究还表明，这些代谢物并非本质上就有益或有害；它们可以产生高度特异性、有时相反的效果。
“这些发现突出了微生物组的矛盾性和复杂性：它不仅影响治疗性免疫系统，也影响肿瘤本身，”Poeck 说。
“通过我们的研究，我们挑战了一个此前占主导地位的观点，并为微生物组研究和基于微生物组疗法的进一步发展开辟了新视角，”Dr. Dr. Markus Perl 说，他是第一作者，也是 University Hospital Regensburg 的医师。从长远来看，这些结果可能有助于通过靶向调节肠道微生物组来改善免疫疗法结局，例如通过微生物群转移或特定饮食策略。
“基于这些发现，我们目前正在 NCT-OCT2 项目中准备一项临床试验 CARBiome，研究在接受过抗生素并计划接受CAR-T细胞疗法的多发性骨髓瘤患者中进行微生物群转移，”Dr. Erik Thiele-Orberg, Ph.D. 说，他是该研究的共同最后作者。
Perl 补充说，这项研究还表明，“Regensburg 科学中心卓越的、具有国际可见度的前沿研究之所以成功，要归功于强有力的合作以及全世界许多敬业科学家的共同努力。”
微生物组研究转向生物活性代谢物
“这些发现将CAR-T细胞疗法中的微生物组研究从纯粹的细菌组成观点转向生物活性代谢物，”Dr. Severin Gütter 和 Dr. Simon Holzinger 解释说，两人都是该研究的共同第一作者。
“我们希望，聚焦细菌代谢物将能够在未来实现更稳健的治疗成功生物标志物。此外，这些代谢物的靶向治疗使用为未来治疗开辟了有趣前景，例如使CAR-T细胞疗法更有效。”
研究团队已经为临床应用提供了初步概念验证：一种基于代谢物的风险评分预测了对CAR-T细胞疗法的临床应答。下一步是与国家和国际伙伴合作，在额外队列中验证这些发现。（生物谷Bioon.com）

title: Blood Cancer Discov：三重靶向＋OX40增强＋6天快速制造！三特异性CAR T细胞疗法为复发难治B细胞血液癌症带来新希望
content:
Blood Cancer Discov：三重靶向＋OX40增强＋6天快速制造！三特异性CAR T细胞疗法为复发难治B细胞血液癌症带来新希望
来源：生物谷原创 2026-10-22 10:02
由俄亥俄州立大学综合癌症中心领导的一项I期临床试验结果显示，可能有一条途径可改善复发或治疗耐药性B细胞血液癌症患者的治疗选择。研究结果发表在Blood Cancer Discovery上。
研究人员得以在早期工作的基础上进一步推进，该早期工作利用CAR T细胞疗法增强B细胞血液癌症的治疗。所有血液癌症中约一半为B细胞血液癌症，包括淋巴瘤和某些白血病。
该试验测试了靶向3种蛋白——CD19、CD20和CD22的三特异性CAR T细胞疗法，并使用一种名为OX40的不同蛋白来增强患者的免疫反应。
“这是CAR T细胞临床试验首次使用OX-40来增强该过程并改善肿瘤杀伤，”该研究第一作者兼通讯作者Sumithira Vasu医学博士说。“我们试验的结果可能为那些B细胞血液癌症复发或治疗停止起效后选择有限的患者带来更好的治疗结局。”
团队还使用了一种更快的流程，在短短6天内完成细胞的采集、制备和回输给患者。这带来了积极结局，且患者副作用极小。
“此前有观点认为新鲜细胞回输更可取，而我们能够证明快速制造时间和新鲜细胞回输的可行性，”共同资深作者LHM项目成员Lapo Alinari医学博士、哲学博士说。“这在B细胞非霍奇金淋巴瘤中产生了有意义的临床活性且副作用极小，并在套细胞淋巴瘤、滤泡性淋巴瘤和弥漫性大B细胞淋巴瘤中实现了缓解。”
CAR T细胞疗法如何工作？
CAR T细胞疗法从患者免疫系统中取出抗癌T细胞，在实验室中修改这些细胞以增强其杀死癌细胞的能力，然后通过输注将细胞回输给患者。
该细胞疗法通常靶向在B细胞血液癌症中起重要作用的CD19蛋白。在此前的动物研究中，其他机构的科学家开发了一种同时靶向另外2种蛋白——CD20和CD22的CAR T细胞疗法，并显示出更强的有效性。
“尽管CAR T细胞疗法已经彻底改变了B细胞血液癌症患者的治疗，缓解率高，但许多患者会在CAR T细胞疗法后复发，且往往在第1年内，”Vasu说。“患者随后只剩下有限的治疗选择。”
该临床试验入组了18名中位年龄为64岁的患者，其中16人接受了OX-40蛋白增强的CAR T细胞过程治疗。所有入组患者在接受增强细胞疗法之前，此前均已接受过中位3种类型的治疗。
“虽然我们的试验显示，接受增强CAR T细胞治疗的B细胞非霍奇金淋巴瘤患者取得了令人鼓舞的结局，但仍需要在更大患者群体中进行更多研究，”资深共同作者Marcos de Lima医学博士说。（生物谷Bioon.com）

content:
派诺生物三款疟疾多阶段疫苗伦理获批，将在澳大利亚启动I期首次人体（First in Human, FIH）临床试验
来源：生物谷 2026-10-22 15:51
Bellberry 人类研究伦理委员会批准派诺生物在澳大利亚开展首次人体临床试验，评估其针对恶性疟原虫和间日疟原虫的多阶段新型U-VLP®疟疾候选疫苗。
Bellberry 人类研究伦理委员会批准派诺生物在澳大利亚开展首次人体临床试验，评估其针对恶性疟原虫和间日疟原虫的多阶段新型U-VLP®疟疾候选疫苗。
派诺生物是一家致力于开发下一代疫苗、以满足全球未满足医疗需求的生物技术公司。公司宣布，其三款多阶段新型U-VLP®疟疾候选疫苗的I期首次人体临床试验（NCT07831226）已于2026年10月19日获得Bellberry 人类研究伦理委员会批准。
其中，LYB014针对恶性疟原虫（Plasmodium falciparum）生命周期中的三个关键阶段；LYB017针对间日疟原虫（Plasmodium vivax）生命周期中的三个关键阶段；而LYB027则同时针对恶性疟原虫和间日疟原虫生命周期中的上述三个关键阶段。这些候选疫苗将联合派诺生物自研的A02佐剂进行评估。A02是一种新型脂质体佐剂，其活性成分均为合成物质。
这项随机、双盲、对照、剂量递增的临床试验将在澳大利亚墨尔本的Nucleus Network Pty Ltd.开展，旨在评估上述疫苗在健康成年志愿者中的安全性和免疫原性。首例受试者入组预计将于2026年12月完成。免疫原性分析将与设于牛津大学儿科学系（Department of Paediatrics）的Draper实验室合作开展。
这些疫苗由派诺生物开发，旨在满足对新一代疟疾疫苗的需求。其设计针对疟原虫生命周期中的三个关键阶段，并期望通过预防感染、发病和传播，为未来消除疟疾的长远目标作出贡献。
尽管全球抗疟工作已取得显著进展，疟疾仍是严峻的全球性公共卫生威胁。2024 年，全球预估疟疾病例 2.82 亿例，死亡 61 万人。绝大多数病例由恶性疟原虫（P. falciparum）和间日疟原虫（P. vivax）两种主要疟原虫引发。两类疟原虫具备复杂的生命周期：携带病原体的蚊虫叮咬人体后，孢子体随之侵入机体并迁移至肝脏完成发育（第一阶段）；随后进入血液循环、入侵红细胞大量增殖（第二阶段）；部分虫体将分化至有性生殖阶段，当蚊虫吸食感染者血液时，虫体进入蚊体内继续发育，继而传播至新宿主（第三阶段）。
目前，世界卫生组织（WHO）批准使用的RTS,S/AS01和R21/Matrix-M疟疾疫苗仅针对恶性疟原虫生命周期的第一阶段，既往在儿童群体开展的 II/III 期临床试验中，仅展现出针对临床疟疾的部分保护效力。LYB014、LYB017和LYB027的研发理念在于探索：同时针对疟原虫生命周期各阶段以及/或覆盖多个疟原虫种类，是否能够提供互补且层次化的保护作用。该科学假说将在后续临床试验中进一步评估。
牛津大学疫苗与转化医学教授Simon Draper表示："我们很高兴能与派诺生物合作，共同开展这项首次人体临床试验的免疫原性分析工作。疟疾仍是全球重大公共卫生挑战，因此有必要持续探索创新疫苗策略，以在疟原虫生命周期的多个阶段提供更广泛、更持久的保护。"
"我们的科研技术有潜力变革抗击疟疾的方式，"派诺生物首席执行官晋博士表示，"我们开发的疟疾疫苗和A02佐剂的目标不仅是预防感染，更是要创造一个更强大、更可负担的防护盾，以应对抗疟原虫复杂的生物学特性，这可能是迈向最终消除疟疾的关键一步。"

小核酸药物在过去五年迎来了管线的爆发式增长，但高速推进的另一面是同样不容忽视的失败率。全球1368个小核酸项目中，处于研发失败、停滞或拒绝上市状态的有455个，失败率约33.3%。2021年以来，259个管线进入失败或停滞状态，其中64.4%终止于药物发现或临床前阶段。更值得深思的是，一些管线在临床试验中成功实现了靶点调控——poly(GP)下降了48%，ATXN2蛋白显著降低，外显子跳跃水平优于已上市药物——却依然未能走到终点。靶点被成功调控，并不意味着疾病进程能够被改变；药效成立之后，安全窗口与产品价值仍决定研发成败。本文内容整理自摩熵咨询《小核酸药物的下一站——全球研发演进、技术迭代与研发成败洞察》报告，结合摩熵医药全球药物研发数据库对全球小核酸项目全生命周期追踪能力，系统梳理近五年研发失败管线的结构性特征与代表性案例。摩熵医药数据库覆盖药物从靶点发现到临床终止的完整信息链条，为行业研究者识别“陷阱靶点”、理解失败逻辑、优化立项决策提供了可验证的数据底座。一、近五年小核酸药物研发失败管线：终止阶段与失败原因分布作为新兴生物技术，小核酸药物的开发仍存在诸多困难。据摩熵医药全球药物研发数据库统计，在全球1368个小核酸药物项目中，处于研发失败、无后续进展、拒绝上市等失败状态的有455个，研发失败率约33.3%。1. 研发失败风险前置近五年行业研发失败的风险呈现明显前置特征，大量管线的终止集中在早期转化与临床价值验证阶段。2021年以来，共有259个研发管线进入了研发失败状态，或是进入超过5年没有任何新进展的停滞状态。从研发终止前的进度来看，有167个管线研发终止于药物发现或临床前阶段，占比达到64.4%，其次是临床II期阶段，终止管线占比15.8%，小核酸药物的研发难点高度集中在早期转化与临床价值验证环节。数据来源：摩熵医药全球药物研发数据库小核酸药物前期研究向正式立项的转化概率较低，候选药物常脱靶导致毒性是重要原因之一。从整体研究终止的原因来看，早期研究未商业化/临床前未推进是占比最大的原因，合计占比32%。根据奥尼兰姆数据，约有40%的Galnac-siRNA候选序列在临床前的大鼠独立筛选阶段中因为肝毒性而被淘汰，而这一肝毒性是siRNA与非目标RNA发生seed区脱靶配对导致的，可见对于小核酸药物，靶向递送与精准识别是药物研发前期阻碍推进的重大壁垒。图片来源：摩熵咨询《小核酸药物的下一站——全球研发演进、技术迭代与研发成败洞察》2. 临床阶段小核酸药物推进壁垒临床阶段小核酸药物最大推进壁垒在于证明其临床价值。从不同研发阶段的终止原因分布来看，药物研发前期（药物发现、临床前）的管线，最常因战略管线优先级调整、早期研究未商业化等原因终止；而进入临床阶段后，因疗效不足、未达主要终点终止的管线占比开始显著上升。即便项目成功完成立项推进到临床，小核酸药物仍容易在临床阶段暴露临床获益不足的问题，这也表明行业在立项前的调研预测工作，仍然存在较大的优化空间。二、小核酸药物研发高失败率靶点分布在近年失败的259个管线中，有83个管线未公布其具体靶点。在剩余有靶点信息的失败管线中，涉及靶点135个，整体靶点集中度较低，较少有明显的“陷阱”靶点。但其中仍有20个靶点的开发失败率超过60%，ICAM1、SCNN1A等9个靶点失败率高达100%，体现出相当高的开发难度。1. DMD：研发热情与失败率双高DMD靶点同时具有高研发热情与高失败率。作为杜氏肌营养不良症的核心靶点，近5年有32个管线针对DMD进行研发，但失败率高达62.5%，有20个管线宣告失败。其中，BioMarin、WAVE Life Sciences曾分别将管线推进至II期与III期临床，但均因疗效不达预期而终止研发。2. TLR9：跨领域开发的高难度样本TLR9靶点作为免疫通路中的关键蛋白，近五年同样拥有较高的研发热情，目标适应症横跨癌症、呼吸系统、胃肠道、炎症、神经系统、免疫调节、皮肤病、肌肉骨骼系统与血液系统等多个领域，但其失败率同样高达62.5%（8个研发管线中5个失败）。Karolinska曾将对应药物cobitollmod推进至III期临床，但因无法达成临床终点而全面终止开发。三、小核酸药物研发失败代表性案例盘点梳理上述失败管线不难发现，两类问题最为典型：其一，靶点被成功调控，并不意味着疾病进程能够被改变；其二，药效成立之后，安全窗口与产品价值仍决定研发成败。以下四个案例，正是这两类困境的缩影。场景一：靶点调控实现，不等于疾病进程得到改善1. 案例一：WVE-004（C9orf72靶点，ASO）WVE-004是Wave Life Sciences开发的一款靶向C9orf72的ASO药物，适应症为C9orf72相关肌萎缩侧索硬化（ALS）和额颞叶痴呆（FTD），最高研发阶段为Phase I/II。C9orf72基因中的六核苷酸重复扩增是ALS和FTD最常见的遗传病因之一，其异常转录产物poly(GP)被认为具有神经毒性。WVE-004的设计逻辑是通过降解含有异常扩增的C9orf72转录本，降低poly(GP)水平，从而减轻神经毒性。临床前研究中，WVE-004能够有效降低患者来源神经细胞的poly-GP，且保留正常转录本；小鼠实验中，药品展现了长期药效，成功降低脊髓与皮层的poly-GP。2022年临床试验中，实验组出现了显著的poly-GP下降，但神经损伤标记NFL及临床功能没有显著改善，公司选择继续推进实验。2023年，在更多患者入组与进行更长期试验后，NFL与临床功能依然没有出现显著改善，公司宣布终止研发。研发时间轴：2018年：临床前研究2021年：启动临床I/II期2023年：临床结束，宣布终止研发失败启示：即使靶点调控获得预期结果，其距离最终疾病获益仍然有着距离。2. 案例二：BIIB105（ION541，ATXN2靶点，ASO）BIIB105是Ionis授权Biogen开发的一款靶向ATXN2的ASO药物，同样用于ALS治疗。ATXN2编码ataxin-2蛋白，其多聚谷氨酰胺扩增与ALS风险相关，被认为通过促进TDP-43蛋白的异常聚集参与疾病进程。临床前小鼠实验中，通过遗传学手段降低ATXN2或使用ATXN2 ASO均能显著降低TDP-43聚集并延长小鼠生存时间，展现出强大的临床潜力。图片来源：摩熵咨询《小核酸药物的下一站——全球研发演进、技术迭代与研发成败洞察》2020年启动的I/II期ALSpire研究（n=99）中，BIIB105实现了脑脊液中ATXN2蛋白的统计学显著降低。然而，在6个月的安慰剂对照期内，BIIB105未能降低血浆神经丝轻链（NfL）水平——NfL是神经退行性变和神经元损伤的标志物。功能、呼吸和肌力等临床终点同样没有改善。在超过40周的开放标签扩展随访中，ATXN2的持续降低并未转化为NfL或临床功能的任何改善。2024年5月，Biogen和Ionis宣布终止BIIB105的开发。研发时间轴：2013年：Ionis授权Biogen开发2020年：启动临床I/II期2024年：宣布终止研发失败原因：靶向机制明确且在人体内展现积极信号，但未能转化为疾病获益。失败启示：与WVE-004类似，即使设计的路径在动物模型中获得了积极结果，靶点调控也达到预期，但距离最终的患者获益仍存在较大差距。小核酸药物的新靶点开发仍然有着巨大的不确定性。场景二：药效达标，安全窗口与产品价值决定研发成败3. 案例三：SRP-5051（DMD外显子51跳跃，肽偶联PMO）SRP-5051（vesleteplirsen）是Sarepta开发的一款多肽偶联PMO（PPMO）药物，通过诱导DMD基因外显子51跳跃、恢复抗肌萎缩蛋白表达来治疗杜氏肌营养不良症。与WVE-004和BIIB105不同，SRP-5051在临床试验中展现了明确的疗效信号。在II期MOMENTUM研究的Part A中，SRP-5051观察到了显著的外显子跳跃和肌营养不良蛋白表达上升，且呈现剂量依赖关系，药物在试验过程中呈现良好的可耐受性，未出现显著的安全性信号。在Part B中，公司继续推高剂量，并于2021年观察到了显著优于已上市外显子跳跃药物的跳跃水平和肌营养不良蛋白表达水平。但随之而来的是安全性问题。早在研究早期，低镁血症（血镁水平偏低）的风险就已被识别，当时被判断为“可监测、可管理”。然而在后续研究中，部分患者出现了持续性的低镁血症，且即使在停药后仍然存在，同时伴有eGFR下降（肾功能指标恶化）。2024年11月，Sarepta宣布终止SRP-5051的开发，理由是长期安全性和耐受性的考量。SRP-5051的失败提供了一个与前述神经领域案例截然不同的教训：当疗效已经成立，安全窗口便成为产品价值的唯一裁判。外显子跳跃水平和肌营养不良蛋白表达的数据是令人鼓舞的，但持续性的低镁血症和肾功能下降意味着药物的治疗窗口过窄——在能够产生疗效的剂量下，安全性风险超出了可接受的范围。这一案例的核心启示在于：对于早期出现的安全性问题，应当尽早评估其剂量依赖性和可逆性，避免在研发后期因安全性风险积累而导致全部投入付诸东流。4. 案例四：Vupanorsen（ANGPTL3靶点，GalNAc-ASO）Vupanorsen是Ionis发现、辉瑞引进的GalNAc-ASO药物，靶向ANGPTL3，适应症为血脂异常与心代谢疾病，最高研发阶段推进至IIb期临床。ANGPTL3是一个经过人类遗传学充分验证的靶点——ANGPTL3功能缺失突变携带者具有较低的LDL-C、甘油三酯水平和冠心病风险。2016年的临床I期试验中，实验组体内ANGPTL3的表达下降83%，同时带来甘油三酯最大平均下降66%、LDL-C最大平均下降35%的显著结果。进入临床IIa期试验后，主要终点再次达标，甘油三酯相较安慰剂组下降约44%，non-HDL-C下降约18%，总胆固醇下降约19%，但LDL-C对比安慰剂组没有出现显著下降，脂肪肝、糖代谢指标等也没有得到显著改善。进入IIb期试验后，在加大药物剂量后获得了更显著的ANGPTL3与甘油三酯下降结果，但non-HDL-C仅下降约22-27.7%，LDL-C仅下降8%-16%，ApoB下降约6-15%，同时加大药量后出现了部分肝脏安全性问题，最终公司宣布终止研发。 研发时间轴：2013年：药物发现2015年：启动临床I期2017年：临床IIa期（高脂血症、脂肪肝）2018年：临床I/II期2019年：辉瑞引进开发2020年：临床IIb期（高脂血症）2022年：宣布终止研发失败原因：尽管证实能够导向临床获益，但获益不足使得药物缺乏继续开发的价值。这款药物的失败留给行业的启示是，即便已经有上市药品Evinacumab证明该靶点整体成药性可行，临床结果也证明药物的作用机制能够带来部分指标改善，但如果最终的临床获益与药物最初的开发期望存在明显差距，不足以支撑药物最终走向上市。结语复盘近五年小核酸失败管线不难发现，研发风险贯穿从临床前到 II 期临床的全流程，失败诱因已经从早期单纯的递送难题，逐步转向靶点生物学验证、分子信号向临床获益转化、安全窗口评估等更深层问题。但失败不是小核酸药物故事的反面，而是它的一部分。对于药企研发人员、项目决策者而言，依托摩熵医药数据库持续对标同靶点、同递送技术、同适应症项目的临床推进节奏与终止案例，读懂靶点冷热与失败底层逻辑，才能在管线立项、临床方案设计阶段识别潜在风险，提升小核酸药物研发的成功率。相关拓展阅读：1. title: 齐鲁制药1类创新生物药QLS2401获批临床，靶向三靶点布局前列腺癌免疫治疗
content:
10月14日，摩熵医药中国药品审评数据库显示，齐鲁制药自主研发的1类创新生物药QLS2401注射液获得国家药品监督管理局药品审评中心（CDE）临床试验默示许可，拟用于治疗转移性去势抵抗性前列腺癌（mCRPC）。图源：摩熵医药-中国药品审评数据库QLS2401是一款同时靶向PSMA、STEAP1和CD3的三特异性T细胞衔接器（TCE）。其通过双肿瘤抗原识别与T细胞募集相结合的设计，探索前列腺癌免疫治疗的新路径。此次获准开展临床试验，意味着QLS2401进入临床开发阶段。其双靶点设计能否在肿瘤抗原表达异质性等情况下展现优势，还有待后续临床研究验证。一、三靶点设计，探索前列腺癌免疫治疗新路径转移性去势抵抗性前列腺癌是前列腺癌治疗中的重要挑战之一，患者仍存在未被满足的治疗需求。QLS2401采用三特异性T细胞衔接器设计，同时识别肿瘤相关抗原PSMA、STEAP1，并结合T细胞表面的CD3，旨在将T细胞募集至肿瘤细胞附近，激活T细胞介导的肿瘤杀伤作用。图源：摩熵医药-全球药物研发数据库与仅针对单一肿瘤抗原的策略相比，PSMA与STEAP1双靶点设计有望提高对不同抗原表达状态肿瘤细胞的识别能力，并降低单一抗原表达下降所导致的免疫逃逸风险。此外，QLS2401还通过优化CD3亲和力及肿瘤抗原结合设计，尝试在增强抗肿瘤活性的同时优化分子特性。不过，这些设计能否转化为更好的疗效和安全性，仍需临床数据进一步验证。二、临床前研究显示潜力，低抗原表达模型值得关注根据现有临床前研究数据，QLS2401在不同抗原表达水平的肿瘤模型中展现出一定的抗肿瘤活性。在PSMA或STEAP1中等、低表达的细胞模型中，QLS2401的杀伤活性优于同类对照分子。在细胞系来源异种移植（CDX）和患者来源异种移植（PDX）肿瘤模型中，该药也表现出抗肿瘤活性，尤其在低抗原表达模型中显示出相对优势。这些结果为QLS2401的双靶点设计提供了临床前依据，也使其在肿瘤抗原表达异质性方面的潜在价值受到关注。但需要指出，临床前模型的结果不能直接预测人体中的疗效。QLS2401能否在患者中实现有效的肿瘤控制，以及其安全性、耐受性和适用人群如何，仍有待临床试验回答。三、今年19款生物药获批临床，齐鲁制药持续拓展创新管线QLS2401的临床获批，也是齐鲁制药今年生物药研发进展的一部分。据相关统计，2026年以来，齐鲁制药已有25余款1类新药获批临床，其中19款为生物药1类新药。上述19款生物药中，13款为首次获批临床的新品，覆盖双靶点融合蛋白、双抗及多抗、抗体偶联药物（ADC）等多个研发方向。

title: 石药集团首款三抗SYS6088与ADC新药SYS6062同日获批临床，晚期实体瘤布局双线加速
content:
10月15日，石药集团宣布，集团开发的SYS6088注射液和SYS6062均获NMPA批准开展临床试验，拟用于晚期实体瘤。图源：企业公告其中，SYS6088是石药集团布局的首个三特异性抗体（以下简称“三抗”），靶向PD-1、VEGFA和CTLA-4。随着这一产品获批临床，石药集团正式进入三抗研发赛道。一、首个三抗获批临床，聚焦三靶点协同SYS6088是一款PD-1/VEGFA/CTLA-4三特异性抗体，本次获批临床拟单药用于晚期/转移性实体瘤。摩熵医药数据库显示，该品种在2026年9月首次申请临床，10月15日，石药集团宣布获批临床。图源：摩熵医药-全球药物研发数据库从作用机制来看，该产品试图通过同时作用于三个靶点，协同调节肿瘤免疫微环境。其中，PD-1和CTLA-4均与T细胞免疫调控有关，VEGFA则参与肿瘤血管生成及肿瘤微环境调节。通过整合上述靶点，SYS6088旨在兼顾解除免疫抑制、促进T细胞活化与扩增，以及抑制肿瘤血管生成等作用。此外，该产品还对Fc端进行了改造，以降低潜在毒性风险并延长药物半衰期。据披露，临床前研究显示，SYS6088在多种恶性肿瘤模型中表现出抗肿瘤活性。至于其多靶点设计能否转化为临床疗效优势，以及安全性是否能够得到验证，仍有待后续临床研究回答。二、三抗与ADC同步推进，石药集团丰富肿瘤管线截至目前，石药集团已有70余款1类新药处于获批临床及以上阶段。除SYS6088外，石药集团另一款新药SYS6062也于同日获NMPA批准在中国开展临床试验，拟用于晚期实体瘤。图源：摩熵医药-中国药品审评数据库SYS6062是一款抗体偶联药物（ADC），通过抗体识别肿瘤细胞相关靶点，将细胞毒性载荷递送至细胞内，以发挥抗肿瘤作用。临床前研究显示，该产品在多种癌症模型中表现出抗肿瘤活性。从三抗到ADC，两款新药采用了不同的抗肿瘤策略。其中，SYS6088聚焦多靶点免疫调节，SYS6062则通过抗体实现细胞毒性载荷的靶向递送。

title: 康缘药业中药1.1类新药十味安肠颗粒获批临床，靶向溃疡性结肠炎新赛道
content:
10月20日，摩熵医药中国药品审评数据库显示，康缘药业联合图锋医药、北峰药业及上海中医药大学申报的中药1.1类新药十味安肠颗粒获批临床，拟用于溃疡性结肠炎。图源：摩熵医药-中国药品审评数据库一、聚焦溃疡性结肠炎，康缘再推创新中药十味安肠颗粒由江苏康缘药业股份有限公司联合上海图锋医药科技有限公司、辽宁北峰药业有限公司及上海中医药大学共同研发，是一款基于中医临床经验方开发的现代中药颗粒制剂。据摩熵医药数据库显示，该药于2026年8月12日首次提交临床试验申请，受理号为CXZL2600075，并于10月20日首次获批临床。图源：摩熵医药全球药物研发数据库此次获批的适应症为溃疡性结肠炎。作为中药1.1类创新药，十味安肠颗粒后续临床研究进展及疗效、安全性数据值得关注。康缘药业在肠道疾病领域已有其他创新中药布局。公司另一款中药1.1类新药健脾疏肝固本颗粒此前已获得临床试验默示许可，拟用于腹泻型肠易激综合征（肝郁脾虚证）。两款产品针对不同适应症，体现了公司在中药创新药领域的持续布局。在成熟中成药方面，康缘药业拥有天舒胶囊、天舒片、苁蓉总苷胶囊等独家产品，属于神经系统疾病用药领域。摩熵医药数据库显示，天舒胶囊2025年全终端销售额超过2亿元，2026年上半年销售额约0.68亿元。

二、超40款中药新药获批生产，今年多款创新药推进临床据摩熵医药数据库显示，截至目前，康缘药业已有超过40款中药新药获批生产。2026年以来，芪黄正气颗粒、车前子片、运脾化痰通窍颗粒等在内的6款中药1类新药已获批临床。图源：摩熵医药-中国药品审评数据库此外，康缘药业还有六味地黄苷糖片、苏辛通窍颗粒、双鱼颗粒等3款中药1.1类新药，以及1款中药2.1类新药热毒宁颗粒报产在审。三、两款化药报产在审，康缘研发管线延伸至化药领域化药领域，康缘药业另有依折麦布阿托伐他汀钙片（Ⅱ）、艾拉莫德片两款仿制药报产在审。图源：摩熵医药-中国药品审评数据库其中，艾拉莫德片值得关注。若后续获批上市，该产品有望成为康缘药业首个上市的抗炎药和抗风湿药。从中药创新药到化药仿制药，康缘药业的研发管线覆盖多个领域。后续相关产品能否顺利推进临床研究、取得注册进展并实现商业化，仍有待进一步观察。

title: NANOBIOTIX公布JNJ-1900 (NBTXR3)联合免疫检查点抑制剂治疗抗PD-1耐药黑色素瘤的I期最终数据【AI生成】
content:
临床阶段生物制药公司NANOBIOTIX在2026年欧洲肿瘤内科学会（ESMO）年会上公布了其正在进行的1100号I期研究的最终更新数据。该研究评估了JNJ-1900 (NBTXR3)联合立体定向放射治疗（SBRT）及免疫检查点抑制剂（nivolumab或pembrolizumab），作为二线及以上疗法，用于治疗经多线治疗失败且对抗PD-1疗法产生耐药的晚期原发性皮肤黑色素瘤患者。在24名重度预处理的患者中，数据显示出可接受的安全性特征及早期疗效信号：根据RECIST 1.1标准，总体缓解率（ORR）为41.7%（含4例完全缓解），疾病控制率（DCR）达75%，中位总生存期（OS）为17.8个月。探索性分析发现，IL-1β是治疗后血浆中增加最多的细胞因子，提示其与治疗诱导的抗肿瘤免疫相关。研究者认为这些初步结果值得在针对抗PD-1初治或难治性黑色素瘤患者的随机临床试验中进一步验证。

10月20日，石药集团宣布，其自主开发的SYH2083滴眼液治疗干眼症的Ⅰ期临床试验（SYH2083-001）已在中国正式启动，目前正推进受试者招募及筛选工作。图源：石药集团企业公告SYH2083是一款靶向淋巴细胞功能相关抗原1（LFA-1）和活性醛类物质（RASP）的双靶点抑制剂。摩熵医药数据库显示，该产品于2026年9月7日首次获批临床，并于10月20日正式启动Ⅰ期临床试验。该产品可抑制LFA-1与细胞间黏附分子-1（ICAM-1）的相互作用，减少LFA-1介导的细胞黏附，同时捕获活性醛类物质。通过双靶点协同作用，该产品有望改善单靶点药物在安全性和有效性方面的局限，为干眼症治疗提供新的潜在选择。图源：摩熵医药-中国药品审评数据库此次启动的SYH2083-001研究是一项在中国健康参与者中开展的单中心、随机、双盲、安慰剂对照、剂量递增Ⅰ期临床试验，主要评估该产品单次及多次给药后的安全性、耐受性和药代动力学特征。随着Ⅰ期临床试验启动，SYH2083将进一步开展早期临床研究，其安全性及药代动力学表现有待后续试验验证。参考来源：[1] 企业公告/官方披露[2] 摩熵医药（原药融云）数据库扩展阅读：1. 石药集团首款三抗SYS6088与ADC新药SYS6062同日获批临床，晚期实体瘤布局双线加速2. 石药集团连发三条研发重磅进展！mRNA肿瘤疫苗、带状疱疹疫苗FDA临床许可、减重单抗Ib期同步落地3. 石药集团SYS6010拟纳入突破性治疗品种，EGFR ADC第4项BTD落地，剑指驱动基因阴性非鳞状NSCLC

小核酸药物正从罕见病与遗传病的小众应用场景，稳步拓展至肿瘤、心血管及代谢疾病等更广阔的疾病治疗版图，是当下创新药研发领域最具发展潜力的方向之一。该类药物以10—50个核苷酸组成的短链核酸分子为活性成分，能够突破传统药物“难以成药”的靶点壁垒，通过降解、沉默或抑制特定基因表达，从源头调控疾病发生机制，同时具备作用效率高、研发周期短、平台可复用等独特优势。当前小核酸药物已形成反义寡核苷酸（ASO）、小干扰 RNA（siRNA）、微小 RNA（miRNA）、适体（Aptamer）四大主流品类。依托化学修饰、GalNAc偶联、LNP包载、抗体/多肽偶联等多元化递送技术的持续迭代，其临床应用边界不断拓宽，全面覆盖肿瘤、眼科疾病、中枢神经系统疾病、遗传及罕见病、心血管及代谢性疾病五大核心领域，全球潜在市场规模约8500亿美元。凭借持续升级的技术体系与不断落地的临床价值，小核酸药物已然成为继小分子药物、抗体药物之后又一值得长期关注的新药研发热点。本文核心内容均摘编自摩熵咨询《小核酸药物的下一站——全球研发演进、技术迭代与研发成败洞察》报告。该报告依托摩熵医药数据库海量生物医药全产业链数据，从技术概览、行业沿革、市场格局、在研管线、终止研发管线等多个维度，系统梳理行业发展全貌，精准研判研发热点与潜在风险，深度挖掘赛道增长潜力。本文结合前沿技术特征与产业落地现状，系统整合并梳理了小核酸药物的技术体系、临床应用场景、主流递送技术及行业发展核心挑战。一、小核酸药物概览：技术分类与核心价值小核酸药物（small nucleic acid drugs）是由10—50个核苷酸构成的短链核酸分子，按药理载荷可分为反义寡核苷酸（ASO）、小干扰RNA（siRNA）、微小RNA（miRNA）与适体（Aptamer）药物等。作为核酸药物的一类，小核酸药物具有作用效率高、研发周期较短等特点，已成为新药研发领域的研究热点。1. 主要分类ASO（反义寡核苷酸）：结构上通常为单链的寡核苷酸；通过与靶RNA序列互补结合，实现RNA降解、剪接调控或翻译阻断的目的。siRNA（小干扰RNA）：通常为双链RNA；经RISC复合物介导，特异性降解靶RNA，实现基因沉默。miRNA（微小RNA）：miRNA类药物可通过模拟或抑制内源性miRNA，调控相关基因表达网络。Aptamer（适体药物）：化学本质常为DNA或RNA，通过特定三维空间构象与靶标结合，蛋白质是目前最常见的靶标。2. 作用机制小核酸药物的作用机制主要分为两类：（1）基因表达调控型：以ASO、siRNA和miRNA为代表，通过靶RNA识别，实现RNA降解或剪接调控，进而改变蛋白表达水平。（2）靶标直接结合型：以适体药物为代表，通过核酸链折叠形成三维构象，直接结合蛋白或细胞等靶标，阻断或调节靶点功能。3. 临床价值这种特殊的作用模式也赋予了小核酸药物显著的临床价值：它能够针对传统药物难以成药的靶点，大幅拓展疾病治疗的边界；序列设计具备天然的平台复用性，企业可以基于同一技术框架快速拓展新靶点与新适应症；在遗传病、罕见病及常见慢性病领域都展现出极高的应用潜力；部分成熟技术路线的产品还能实现数月一次的长效给药，部分前沿研究甚至在向接近一次性治疗的目标推进。4. 关键挑战目前小核酸药物行业仍处于高速发展期，技术落地与产业化仍面临多重瓶颈。首先，药物有效成分体内稳定性不足，极易被体内核酸酶降解，直接影响药效发挥；其次，组织与细胞特异性递送是行业核心技术瓶颈，严重制约药物生物利用率与靶向精准度；再次，药物应用存在脱靶效应、非特异性免疫激活及长期安全性未知等风险，临床应用安全性仍需持续验证；最后，药物生产工艺复杂，生产成本、质量控制及规模化量产的技术标准严苛，产业化门槛较高。整体来看，未来小核酸药物的行业竞争，将集中聚焦于靶点精准筛选、高效递送技术突破、用药安全性优化三大核心方向。二、小核酸药物的主要治疗领域小核酸药物横跨肿瘤、眼科疾病、中枢神经系统、遗传病及罕见病、心血管及代谢性疾病五大市场，潜在市场规模约8500亿美元，展现出广阔的应用潜力。图片来源：摩熵咨询《小核酸药物的下一站——全球研发演进、技术迭代与研发成败洞察》心血管及代谢性疾病（2400亿美元市场）：高胆固醇血症、高甘油三酯血症、高血压、血栓疾病等。遗传病及罕见病（2358亿美元市场）：血友病A/B、遗传性血管性水肿、肝性卟啉症、家族性淀粉样变多发性神经病等。中枢神经系统（334亿美元市场）：肌萎缩侧索硬化、运动神经元病等。眼科疾病（600亿美元市场）：地图状萎缩、年龄相关性黄斑变性、湿性年龄相关性黄斑变性、巨细胞病毒视网膜炎等。肿瘤（2864亿美元市场）：骨髓发育异常综合征、胰腺癌等。其他：角膜移植排斥、慢性疲劳综合征等。目前，小核酸药物已经在心血管及代谢性疾病、遗传病、罕见病等领域展现出较高的应用潜力。以肌萎缩侧索硬化（渐冻症）为例，该疾病由超氧化物歧化酶1（SOD1）基因突变引发，传统药物研发长期陷入困境，核心原因是SOD1蛋白结构高度稳定，无适配传统药物结合的作用位点，始终缺乏有效治疗手段。而小核酸药物托夫生（Tofersen）可直接靶向致病基因与RNA，从疾病根源干预病情发展，为渐冻症治疗开辟全新路径。该药物于2023年获批上市，2024年正式进入中国市场，落地惠及国内罕见病患者，充分印证了小核酸药物的独特临床价值。三、小核酸药物的主要递送方式递送技术被普遍视为小核酸药物研发的核心胜负手。当前上市产品以化学修饰及GalNAc偶联最为常见，同时以LNP（脂质纳米颗粒）及抗体/多肽偶联探索肝外靶向。1. 化学修饰直接给药主要用于ASO与适体药物，常见给药部位为玻璃体内、鞘内、皮下与局部。其核心逻辑是依靠PS／2’位修饰或PEG化增强稳定性，无需复杂载体。作为最成熟的技术路线，它特别适合局部用药或可直接到达靶组织的场景，代表药品包括Fomivirsen、Nusinersen、Tofersen（托夫生）与Pegaptanib。2. GalNAc偶联主要用于以siRNA为主、部分ASO的药物，靶向肝细胞ASGPR，可实现皮下注射、低频给药与明确的肝靶向，是当前肝靶向小核酸的核心平台。代表产品包括Givosiran、Lumasiran、Inclisiran（英克司兰钠）、Vutrisiran与Eplontersen。3. LNP包载主要用于以siRNA为主、部分miRNA及双链RNA的探索。其递送逻辑是包载保护核酸，促进细胞摄取与内体逃逸，适用于需要系统给药、需要额外包载保护的RNA载荷。其系统性递送验证充分，但产品数量少于GalNAc，代表产品为Patisiran。4. 抗体/多肽偶联主要用于ASO与siRNA，目标是突破肝外组织，聚焦肌肉、心肌及中枢神经系统；其核心价值在于利用受体介导内吞实现细胞定向递送。该路线临床推进较快，是肝外递送的重要方向，代表在研项目包括Del-desiran（AOC 1001）、DYNE-101等。需要补充的是，化学修饰是多数小核酸药物的技术基础，与LNP或偶联策略并非互斥关系——GalNAc-siRNA、LNP-siRNA通常同样采用2’位修饰及磷硫酰键等化学修饰手段。递送方式的演进也并非简单的代际替代，而是在用药便利性、靶向可及目标等方向上的持续拓展。除上述四种方式外，外泌体、无机纳米颗粒（金、氧化铁、硅等）等多种递送策略也处于探索之中。结语从首个反义药物问世，到GalNAc技术平台的成熟，再到抗体偶联递送向肝外组织进军，小核酸药物已完成从“概念验证”到“商业化兑现”的关键跨越。展望未来，靶点选择的精准化、递送系统的组织拓展化、化学修饰与安全性优化的持续迭代，将共同决定这一赛道的下一批赢家。对于身处其中的研发者与决策者而言，唯有建立在对全球研发数据持续追踪与深入洞察之上的判断，才能在技术迭代与研发成败交织的浪潮中把握先机。资料来源：1. title: 南京正大天晴左卡尼汀咀嚼片获批上市！斩获国内首仿+首家过评，撬动超6亿元市场
content:
10月15日，NMPA官网显示，南京正大天晴制药申报的左卡尼汀咀嚼片获批上市，成为该剂型国内首仿。摩熵医药数据库显示，2026年上半年，左卡尼汀相关剂型在全终端销售额超过6亿元。在这一市场规模下，咀嚼片剂型迎来首家国内企业获批，南京正大天晴进一步丰富了其仿制药产品矩阵。图源：NMPA官网一、超6亿元市场，咀嚼片剂型迎来首仿左卡尼汀是一种参与人体能量代谢的药物，主要作用是促进长链脂肪酸进入线粒体进行β-氧化，为心肌、骨骼肌等组织提供能量。其原研企业为意大利阿尔法西格玛公司，左卡尼汀于1990年获得美国FDA批准上市，左卡尼汀注射液原研产品于1999年在国内上市。摩熵医药数据库显示，左卡尼汀注射液、片剂、口服溶液等相关剂型，2026年上半年全终端销售额超过6亿元，已形成一定的市场规模。

content:
加拿大英属哥伦比亚大学Josef M. Penninger团队在《Cell Stem Cell》发表研究，针对1型糖尿病治疗中干细胞来源胰岛类器官（PIOs）因血管化不足导致移植后β细胞大量死亡的难题，提出新解决方案。研究人员利用人血管类器官（BVOs）与干细胞来源胰岛共培养，构建出带有器官特异性毛细血管网络的血管化胰岛类器官（VPIOs）。研究发现，β细胞分泌的VEGFA驱动内皮细胞获得“窗孔”结构等胰岛特异性特征，而血管细胞分泌的BMP4促进β细胞成熟并增强其抗缺氧能力。在糖尿病小鼠模型中，皮下移植VPIOs实现了长期血糖正常化，疗效与原代人胰岛相当，显著优于未血管化类器官。该研究揭示了胰岛细胞与血管的双向互作机制，为干细胞来源胰岛移植提供了新策略，但也指出需进一步解决外分泌细胞残留、临床基质替代及体外成熟度等问题。

title: [Correspondence] Prioritising the future of youth is an urgent political choice
summary: Health professionals and policy makers should fully support the students currently protesting in France.1 Apart from the regrettable outbursts of violence happening during protests, this movement reflects the anger of youth at decades of successive policies, both at national and global levels, which have progressively widened educational inequalities. These educational inequalities have led to a cascade of further inequalities: access to employment and type of employment (manual or office-based); level of income—in the past 20 years, the Gini index in France increased from 0·27 to 0·30;2 living conditions and the environment (quality of food, water, noise, air, etc); and, eventually, health inequities.

title: [Comment] The role of product safety and liability law in governing digital determinants of health

title: [Correspondence] China–Nepal border catastrophic floods: a planetary health alarm
summary: The Hindu Kush Himalayan region, also known as the Third Pole, is warming faster than the global average, with mountain environments experiencing particularly rapid climatic change and climatic extremes.1 The potential risks of glacial lake outburst floods (GLOFs) have been documented for decades, with 47 glacial lakes at risk of expansion and causing GLOFs located in the Hindu Kush Himalayan region, including 21 in Nepal.2 The Rasuwa-Bhote Koshi flood of Aug 26, 2026, near the China–Nepal border, resulted in a catastrophic flood travelling at a speed of 188 km/h from its source; the flood covered 20 km within 7–8 min and reached the China–Nepal border at Rasuwagadhi.
